newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's 1999 polls could be postponed--officials.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's 1999 polls could be postponed--officials.

text.p: South Africa's second all-race general elections were unlikely to go ahead as scheduled in 1999, the head of the local government elections task group told the Sunday Independent newspaper.

"By my calculations we are running a year behind schedule if we want to hold proper elections," Frederick van Zyl Slabbert told the paper, adding that the government had left the appointment of an electoral commission for too late.
He said the foot-dragging made it almost impossible for the commission to complete its main task of drawing up a proper voters' roll and demarcating voting districts before the 1999 deadline.
Even if the appointment of the commission were given priority, it would probably not be up and running before the end of the year, Slabbert said.

Judge Johan Kriegler -- who headed the electoral commission in the country's 1994 historic first all-race polls in which President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress swept to victory -- added his voice to the concern.
"It is very urgent for those in power to consider the risk we are running if the election in 1999 is not given timeous planning."

The Sunday Independent said both Slabbert and Kriegler had alerted cabinet ministers to the impending crisis, but were doubtful whether the commission would have more than a year to organise the elections.

The men said postponing the elections would be disastrous as the constitution would have to be changed. But it would also be impossible to run the elections without a proper voter's roll and demarcated voting districts.
"Cancelling the elections is not an option, but its credibility and soundness is definitely an issue," Slabbert said.
Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana told the Sunday Independant the cabinet had "not yet even considered the 1999 elections".

"It is totally premature to cast judgement now on an event due to take place in two years' time. Take the 1994 election. This was decided upon in 1993. We were able to pull this together at very short notice."
